planner.question: Can a witness-separated universal rejection encoding settle the augmented-resolution transfer premise without assuming polynomial SAT algorithms produce proofs?

planner.alternative: Construct a compact diamond-chain rejector with exponentially many minimal rejected inputs.
planner.stop_rule: If reflection certificates provably inherit resolution lower bounds, reject the short-reflection premise for that calculus; do not infer P!=NP.

construct.claim: Witness-separated reflection augmentation is polynomially equivalent to ordinary resolution on normalized 3CNF, and reflection length dominates every rejected instance's resolution length.
construct.scope: Explicit width-three clause pool, unary clock, deterministic rejection circuit independent of satisfying witness; ordinary resolution.
construct.derivation: Fix presence and all computation gate bits to a rejecting execution; every gate clause disappears and guarded clauses become exactly the input; restrict refutation.
unresolved_steps: Unrestricted lower bound and a noncircular simulation theorem for a different model.
candidate_tests: Replay reflection refutations and exact specializations for every rejected small diamond input.

alternative.claim: Diamond-chain Horn rejection has exponential positive-DNF core-cover size but linear-size resolution reflection proofs.
alternative.scope: Specified implication pool and monotone rejection circuit.
alternative.derivation: Two alternative paths per segment; 2^k minimal subsets; guarded path propagation combines at each OR gate.
unresolved_steps: General computation lower bounds; no general circuit lower bound.
candidate_tests: Enumerate small presence subsets and source models; produce large compact proofs and reject corrupt traces.
